title: Router
description: A machine of yours as this network's router.
intro: Turn one of your Linux machines into this network's router. Lines bring the internet in; networks give your devices addresses.
noMachinesBody: Add a Raspberry Pi or a computer running Linux, with root access, and it will appear here.
noRoot: Polaris has no root access on these machines. Remove one and add it again with root access.
portsHint: What is plugged in, and which lines and networks ride each port.
linesHint: Tried in this order. If one fails, the next takes over and the first returns when it recovers.
networksHint: Each network has its own subnet, addresses and rules.
networkBody: Devices on this port get an address automatically.
name: Name
badSubnet: Use a 10.x.x.x or 192.168.x.x subnet between /16 and /29.
badAddress: It must be an address inside the subnet.
internetHint: Off keeps these devices off the internet.
isolateHint: Devices here reach no other network, nor this machine's login.
forwardsHint: Let the internet reach a device. Everything else stays closed.
forwardBody: Only works on a line that takes visitors.
clientsHint: Devices holding an address from this router.
lineBody: How this line reaches the internet. Your provider gives you these details.
ipv6Hint: Public IPv6 for these devices, if the first line offers a prefix.
wifiHint: Broadcast this network from the radio on this port.
wifiCountryHint: Two letters, like ES. It sets what the radio may legally use.
sessionDown: Not signed in yet. Check the user and password, and that the modem is in bridge mode.
notAiring: Wi-Fi is not on the air. This radio may not work as an access point on that band.
noPrefix: No IPv6 yet. The first line is not offering a prefix.
noPrefixClient: No IPv6 yet. This machine could not install dhcpcd, which IPv6 needs. Press Apply to try again.

problems.sharedPort: Two lines or networks use the same port untagged. Give one of them a VLAN tag.
problems.overlap: Another network already uses this subnet.
problems.outside: That address is in none of these networks.
problems.badReservation: A network has a fixed address that cannot be used. Edit that network.
problems.badPort: One of these ports cannot be used. Choose another.
problems.badStaticLine: The gateway must be inside the line's subnet, written like 203.0.113.2/29.
problems.lineSubnet: A network uses the same subnet as a fixed line. Choose another subnet.
problems.badPppoe: A PPPoE line needs a user. Edit that line.
problems.badWifi: Use a name up to 32 bytes, a password of 8 to 63 characters, and a two-letter country.
problems.wifiVlan: Wi-Fi cannot run on a VLAN. Remove the VLAN from this network.
problems.badVlan: A VLAN is a number from 2 to 4094.

cannotRead: Polaris cannot read this machine right now.
clientsLimited: Showing {shown} of {total}. Search to narrow them down.
clientsCapped: Only the first {max} devices are read from the machine.
badReservation: Use a MAC like aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff and a free address inside the subnet, each used once.
badOpenPort: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
applyBody: Its network changes and connected devices may drop for a moment. If Polaris cannot reach it again within 2 minutes, the machine goes back by itself.
stopBody: Devices behind it lose their network. The machine goes back to normal.
lineMissing: This port is not on the machine. Check that it is plugged in.
lineNoWay: No internet from this port yet. Check the cable and that the line gives out an address.
wentBack: The last change did not hold and was undone

errors.generic: That did not work. Try again.
errors.invalid: Check the values marked in the form.
errors.noRoot: Polaris has no root access on this machine. Remove it and add it again with root access.
errors.unreachable: This machine is not answering. Check that it is on and connected.
errors.unsupported: This system is not supported yet. Use Debian, Ubuntu or Raspberry Pi OS.
errors.missingPort: One of those ports is not on this machine any more. Choose it again.
errors.lineOverlap: A network uses the same subnet as a line. Choose another subnet.
errors.notRadio: That port has no radio, so it cannot run Wi-Fi.
errors.noPassword: A line or Wi-Fi network has no password. Edit it and type one.
errors.lockout: Polaris reaches this machine through that port, so it would lose it. Choose another port, or use a VLAN.
errors.rolledBack: The change did not hold, so the machine went back. Nothing changed.
errors.unconfirmed: Polaris lost this machine during the change. It should already be back on its previous setup.

modelTitle: How a router is set up here
modelLines: An internet line is the port your modem or provider cable is plugged into. With several, the next takes over when one fails.
modelNetworks: A network is a group of devices with its own subnet, such as Home, Guests or Cameras. The router hands out their addresses and is their gateway.
modelVlans: One port carries one untagged link. To put more networks on the same cable, give each a VLAN tag and set the same tag on the switch.
modelApply: Nothing changes on the machine until Apply, and a change that cuts Polaris off is undone by itself.
vlanNumberHint: A number from 2 to 4094. The switch port or modem on this cable must use the same tag.
lineVlanHint: Leave untagged unless your provider gave you a VLAN number for this line.
lanVlanHint: Untagged for devices plugged straight in or into a plain switch.
vlanHelp: A VLAN tag is a number added to each packet so one cable can carry several separate networks. A laptop or a plain switch only sends untagged traffic, so each port can have one untagged line or network.
vlanHelpSwitch: Tagged networks reach devices through a managed switch or access point: set the same VLAN as tagged on the port that goes to this machine, and as untagged on the ports where the devices plug in.
untaggedTaken: {port} untagged is already used by {who}. Choose VLAN, or another port.
vlanTaken: VLAN {vlan} on {port} is already used by {who}. Choose another number.
clashUntagged: {port} untagged is used by both {first} and {second}.
clashVlan: VLAN {vlan} on {port} is used by both {first} and {second}.
clashWhy: The machine cannot tell their traffic apart, so this cannot be applied.
clashFixNote: Then set VLAN {vlan} as tagged on the switch port that {port} is plugged into.
clashLines: Give one of these lines the VLAN your provider uses, or move it to another port.
onePortBody: If {port} is the internet line, networks can only share it on a VLAN, which needs a managed switch. For plain devices, add a second port, such as a USB Ethernet adapter.
onePortLine: It already brings the internet in, so a network can only share it on a VLAN, through a managed switch with the same tag. For plain devices, add a second port, such as a USB Ethernet adapter.
noLines: No lines yet. Add the port your modem or provider cable is plugged into.
linePortHint: The port the modem or provider cable is plugged into.
lineModeHint: Automatic works with most modems. The other two only if your provider gave you their details.
lineAddressHint: From your provider, with its prefix, like 203.0.113.2/29.
lineGatewayHint: Your provider's side of the line, inside that subnet.
lineUserHint: From your provider. The modem has to be in bridge mode.
noNetworks: No networks yet. Add one for the devices behind this router.
lanPortHint: The port the devices, or their switch, are plugged into.
subnetRoom: {count, plural, one {Room for # device} other {Room for # devices}}
routerAddressHint: Devices use it as gateway and DNS. Usually the first address.
dhcpSummary: Devices get an address from {first} to {last} on their own, with this router as gateway and DNS. Leases last 12 hours.
subnetHelpTitle: What do I put in subnet?
subnetHelp: The range of addresses this network uses. 10.77.1.0/24 means 10.77.1.1 to 10.77.1.254: the /24 is how many addresses it holds (/24 is 254, /23 is 510, /16 is 65534). Each network needs its own range, and it must not match the one your modem uses.
reservationsHint: Always give the same address to a device, by its MAC. Needed for an open port.
noForwards: Nothing is open. Every connection from the internet is refused.
protocolHint: TCP for web and most apps. UDP for games, calls and VPNs.
openPortHint: The port visitors reach on your public address, like 443.
toAddressHint: A device in one of your networks, like {example}. Give it a fixed address first.
unsaved: Changes not applied yet. The machine keeps its current setup until Apply.
rollbackNote: Each Apply is undone by itself if Polaris cannot reach the machine within {seconds} seconds.
notRouterBody: Add an internet line and a network, then Apply.
countForwards: {count, plural, one {# open port} other {# open ports}}
